text: This script connects straight to the warehouse using sqlalchemy and pyodbc, then reads the fact table and dimensions directly into pandas DataFrames — the same real connection pattern used to reach SQL Server from Python anywhere else in this catalog.

The orphan check is a set difference: every key the fact table actually uses, minus every key the dimension actually has. Whatever's left over is a foreign key that doesn't resolve to a real dimension row — exactly the failure mode a late schema change or a bypassed constraint can cause.
Four checks, four real pandas techniques: len of the DataFrame for row-count parity, isna-sum for unexpected nulls, duplicated for repeated rows, and the set difference for orphaned keys.
Next lesson schedules this exact script to run every night, unattended, and logs its result so a human only has to look when something actually fails.
